commit.message:
Make the WebMCP polyfill internal (#834)

installWebMcpPolyfill was exported from the SDK's main entry point as a
convenience for WebMCP-authored views running where neither the browser
nor the host provides document.modelContext. Such views should bring
their own polyfill instead: the SDK's copy exists to back its own tests
of the WebMCP -> Apps bridge, and keeping it public would commit the
SDK to maintaining a faithful WebMCP implementation.

- Remove the re-export from src/app.ts (the export never shipped in a
  release; it was added after v2.0.4)
- Import it directly from ./webmcp-polyfill.js in the interop test
- Mark the function @internal and reword the module header
- Reword the draft spec's bridging paragraph to match

Co-authored-by: ochafik <ochafik@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
pdf-server: validate annotations with per-type schemas (#832)

Stamps often rendered as the literal text "undefined": the annotation
arrays were typed z.record(z.string(), z.any()), so a stamp sent with
content (note/freetext's field) instead of label sailed through, and
every render path coerced the missing label — textContent and fillText
drew "undefined" and the save path baked it into the PDF bytes.

Replace the loose shape with strict per-type zod schemas shared by both
tool surfaces (new src/annotation-schemas.ts): a discriminated union for
add_annotations (stamp requires label, note/freetext require content,
image requires imageUrl or imageData, unknown keys are errors rather
than silent strips) and a partial union for update_annotations (id and
type required, text fields clearable to "", imported annotations accept
position patches). The app tools enforce them through their input
schemas; the server-mediated interact validates per def and names the
failing index, type and field. Compile-time guards assert each schema's
output against its pdf-annotations.ts interface so the two cannot
drift silently.

The render and save paths also get explicit fallbacks (label ?? STAMP,
content ?? "") so annotations persisted before this validation no
longer draw "undefined" or throw while saving. Tool descriptions fix
the rects shorthand ({x,y,w,h} -> {x,y,width,height}) that the schemas
now enforce.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Bridge App-registered tools and WebMCP in both directions (middle ground for #797) (#829)

* Bridge App-registered tools and WebMCP in both directions

Keep App.registerTool and the tools/list / tools/call channel as they are,
and make the two tool surfaces interoperable:

- Tools registered with App.registerTool are mirrored into
  document.modelContext when the document provides one, so WebMCP-enabled
  hosts discover them without speaking the Apps tools channel.
- Tools the page registers on document.modelContext are served over
  tools/list / tools/call (declaring the tools capability when the page
  carries WebMCP tools at connect time), with toolchange relayed as
  notifications/tools/list_changed, so WebMCP-authored views work on
  MCP Apps hosts.
- installWebMcpPolyfill() gives WebMCP-authored views a drop-in
  document.modelContext where neither the browser nor the host provides
  one.

Registered tools shadow same-named WebMCP entries, which also keeps a
tool's own mirror from being listed twice; only the frame's own tools are
served. Both behaviors can be switched off per App
(mirrorToolsToWebMcp / bridgeWebMcpTools).

* Replace the per-direction WebMCP opt-outs with one webMcpBridge option

Collapse mirrorToolsToWebMcp/bridgeWebMcpTools into a single
webMcpBridge?: boolean (default true) that switches the whole two-way
bridge off. Nobody has asked for per-direction control, and the shape
can widen compatibly later (boolean -> boolean | object, as autoResize
did) if someone does.

Also forward webMcpBridge through useApp (previously only
autoResize/strict reached the App), add a test that webMcpBridge: false
disables both directions, and register test pairs for cleanup before
connecting so a failed connect does not leak into later tests.

Co-authored-by: ochafik <ochafik@anthropic.com>

* style: fix prettier formatting in webmcp.ts

Co-authored-by: ochafik <ochafik@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
pdf-server: default to a single interact app tool (#830)

Thirteen per-action app tools meant thirteen approval cards on hosts
that ask the user to approve each app tool separately. Fold them into
one interact app tool mirroring the server-side interact: an action
enum plus flat parameters, an optional commands batch with the same
contract (content[i] per commands[i], a failed step's slot starts with
ERROR, no isError on multi-step batches since some host SDKs collapse
isError results to content[0].text), and per-action validation from
the same zod schemas the split tools used.

The per-action tools stay available behind a new --split-app-tools
CLI flag: the server injects a one-line config script into the served
view HTML (cached alongside the base bundle), which the view reads
before connect(). get-document-info becomes get_document_info so the
action enum is uniformly snake_case.

Tests: unit coverage for the config injection (skipped when the view
bundle is not built, as in the publish workflow's test job), a new
e2e spec driving the app-side interact end to end (listing, dispatch,
validation, batch, mid-batch failure), and pdf-page-restore.spec.ts
migrated to the interact surface with the frame/JSON-RPC helpers
extracted to tests/e2e/pdf-app-helpers.ts instead of a third copy.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Security: bump solid-js override to 1.9.17 and refresh vulnerable transitives (#827)

* Security: bump solid-js override to 1.9.17 and refresh vulnerable transitives

npm audit went red again since the Sep 25 cleanup (#793): 24
advisories, 8 critical, mostly in-range transitive fixes.

- solid-js override 1.9.15 -> 1.9.17 (seroval fromJSON/TypedArray
  advisories; same mechanism as the #793 pin, new advisory)
- sharp ^0.35.3 -> ^0.35.5 (librsvg CVE-2026-96889)
- lockfile-only refresh of the other vulnerable transitives within
  existing ranges: shell-quote 1.12.0, proxy-addr 2.0.8, body-parser
  2.4.0, zod 4.6.6, source-map-js 1.2.2, ip-address 10.7.4, hono
  4.13.13, vite 6.4.4, @vue/server-renderer 3.5.43 and their solid
  toolchain companions

Not included: undici 7.30.1, fast-uri 3.1.9, markdown-it 14.3.3
(releases too fresh to validate in this environment) and the
@modelcontextprotocol/* 2.x pin bumps, which deserve their own PR.

Validated: npm install from the updated lockfile, npm run build, and
the SDK unit suite (349 tests) all pass.

Co-authored-by: ochafik <ochafik@anthropic.com>

* Match basic-server-solid's solid-js pin to the 1.9.17 override

npm requires a direct dependency and its override to share the same
spec; bumping only the root override left the workspace pinned at
1.9.15, so npm ci rejected the lockfile (missing solid-js@1.9.15,
seroval@1.5.6) and every CI job failed at install. Verified npm ci
--dry-run passes on both npm 10 and npm 11.

Co-authored-by: ochafik <ochafik@anthropic.com>

* style: auto-fix prettier formatting

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: github-actions[bot] <github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Fix pdf-server saved-page restore (dead pageCount guard since #329) (#828)

* Fix pdf-server saved-page restore: dead pageCount guard since #329

The viewer saves the current page to localStorage and is meant to
restore it when a host re-renders the same tool call, but the restore
bounds-checked the saved page against structuredContent.pageCount — a
field display_pdf stopped sending in #329 (the server no longer
pre-parses the PDF). The comparison was always false, so the viewer
always fell back to initialPage: annotations survived a re-render,
the page never did.

- Restore the saved page unconditionally and clamp to totalPages once
  the document loads (same clamp reloadPdf already has).
- Resolve viewUUID from _meta with a structuredContent fallback: the
  server sends it in both, and some hosts drop _meta on replayed tool
  results — without the fallback the page had no storage key at all.
- Drop the pageCount field from the parsed-result type (never sent).

The e2e test plays the host: it captures the display_pdf result from
the result panel, navigates via the view's tool, re-posts the result
as a ui/notifications/tool-result notification, and asserts the viewer
comes back on the saved page — with and without _meta.

* style: auto-fix prettier formatting

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: github-actions[bot] <github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
